source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assign responsibility for unresolved unit problems to the departing nurse after the resignation is final","B":"Collect candid feedback about the work experience and reasons for leaving to identify improvement opportunities","C":"Prevent the employee from leaving by requiring withdrawal of the resignation during the interview","D":"Replace retention analysis because one exit interview is sufficient to explain all staff turnover patterns"}}
source_row.rationale: Exit interviews can collect feedback about why employees leave and reveal workplace, management, training, culture, or retention issues. Organizations should analyze the information as one input for improvement rather than treating it as proof of a single cause.
source_row.source_detail: Current SHRM discussion accessed 2026-08-14: exit interviews gather information about why employees leave and can inform retention and organizational improvement efforts.
source_row.source_name: SHRM — What Can Exit Interviews Teach Us About Employee Retention?
source_row.stem: What is a useful organizational purpose of an exit interview with a departing nurse?
